ai.headline: Amazon now shares ad value estimates and identifiers with ad companies
ai.summary: Amazon's privacy policy now says it may share an advertising identifier and an estimate of the value of ads shown to you with ad companies, while stating it does not share your specific shopping actions such as purchases, product views, or searches. Several links were also renamed: ad preferences now point to a "Your Ads Privacy Choices" page, and data access or deletion requests now go through "Data Privacy Queries" instead of Customer Service.

ai.headline: Amazon now uses customer data to develop and deploy its generative AI models
ai.summary: Amazon's privacy policy now says it uses your personal information, including data used to improve its services, to develop or deploy its generative AI models and services, and it points to a separate Generative AI Development Disclosure for details. The policy does not say whether an opt-out is available, so the change means your data may now help train Amazon's AI.
